content.title: What are Abstraction and Encapsulation?
content.description: Abstraction and Encapsulation are two fundamental principles of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP). Abstraction focuses on hiding implementation details, while Encapsulation focuses on protecting data by combining it with methods.

content.content: Abstraction helps users focus only on what an object does instead of how it works. Encapsulation bundles data and methods into a single unit (class) while restricting direct access to the data. Together, they make Java applications secure, modular, and easier to maintain.

content.title: Why Learn These Concepts?
content.content: Abstraction simplifies complex systems, while encapsulation improves security, maintainability, and data integrity. Both are essential pillars of Object-Oriented Programming.
Understanding Abstraction
Abstraction hides implementation details and exposes only the essential functionality to the user. Users interact with an object through its interface without knowing how the internal logic works.

content.title: Key Idea of Abstraction
content.description: Focus on what an object can do instead of how it performs the task.

content.content: Real-Life Example of Abstraction

content.title: Driving a Car
content.content: When driving a car, you use the steering wheel, accelerator, and brakes without knowing how the engine or transmission works internally. This is abstraction.
How Abstraction is Achieved
Java provides abstraction using abstract classes and interfaces. They define what operations should be performed without specifying every implementation detail.

content.title: Abstract Class Example

content.content: Understanding Encapsulation
Encapsulation combines data (variables) and methods into a single class while restricting direct access to internal data. This is achieved using private variables and public getter/setter methods.
Private Variables
Instance variables are usually declared as private so they cannot be accessed directly from outside the class.
Getter and Setter Methods
Getter methods read private data, while setter methods modify private data in a controlled manner.

content.content: Advantages of Encapsulation

items.question: Controlled Modification
items.answer: Setter methods can validate data before storing it.

items.question: Better Maintainability
items.answer: Internal implementation can change without affecting users.

items.question: Code Reusability
items.answer: Encapsulated classes are easier to reuse in different applications.

content.content: Abstraction vs Encapsulation

left_points: Achieved using abstract classes and interfaces
right_points: Achieved using private fields and getters/setters

content.content: Real-Life Comparison

content.title: ATM Machine
content.content: Using an ATM is an example of abstraction because users only interact with the screen without knowing the internal banking process. The customer's account details are protected using encapsulation, as direct access to bank data is not allowed.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers commonly ask the differences between abstraction and encapsulation, along with questions about abstract classes, interfaces, access modifiers, getters, setters, and data hiding.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Is abstraction the same as encapsulation?
items.answer: No. Abstraction hides implementation details, whereas encapsulation hides internal data.

items.question: Can private variables be accessed directly?
items.answer: No. They should be accessed through public getter and setter methods.

items.question: Can an abstract class be instantiated?
items.answer: No. Objects cannot be created directly from an abstract class.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Abstraction hides complexity, while encapsulation hides data. Together they improve software design, security, and maintainability.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Abstract classes and interfaces support abstraction.
Private variables and getters/setters support encapsulation.
Both concepts improve code quality and maintainability.
